1. This Ordinance may be cited as the Notaries Public
Ordinance, 1959, and shall come into force on such date as
the Yang di-Pertuan Agong may by notification in the

Gazette appoint. In fore /- 10.59 - EN SI 6/4

2. In this Ordinance, unless | the context otherwise
requires—

"Bar Council" means the central council of the Bar
elected under sections 42, 43 and 44 of the Advocates and
Solicitors Ordinance, 1947;

"notary public" means a person who has been appointed
as a notary public under section 3} but does not include any
person whose appointment has been revoked under section 5.

3. (1) The Attorney-General may, from time to time,
appoint fit and proper persons to be notaries public to
practise within the Federation ori such territory within the
Federation as may be specified in the appointment.

(2) No person shall be appointed to be a notary public
unless he is a practising advo¢ate and solicitor of the
Supreme Court

Provided that in any place in which a suitable advocate
and solicitor is not available for appointment, the Attorney-
General may, in his discretion, appoint a public officer to be
a notary public, and any fees received by a public officer
so appointed in respect of his functions as a notary public
shall be paid into the Treasury.

(3) The Attorney-General shall not make any appoint-
ment under this section without consulting the Bar Council.

(4) In making any appointment under this section the
Attorney-General shall have regard to the number of
notaries public already practising in the place where the
applicant proposes to practise and to the convenience of the
inhabitants of such place, but, subject as aforesaid, the
Attorney-General shall have absolute discretion in making or
refusing to. make any such appointment and there shall be
no appeal from his decision.

(S) If it shall appear to the Attorney-General that any
notary public is about to be absent from the Federation
for a period exceeding one month, the Attorney-General
may appoint any person, beihg a practising advocate and
solicitor of the Supreme Court, to be a notary public
temporarily during the absen¢e of such notary public from
the Federation.

(6) No temporary appointment of a notary public shall
have effect for a longer period than twelve months and any
such appointment shall lapse pn the death or on the return
to the Federation of the notary public on account of whose
departure from the Federation such appointment was made.

(7) Every appointment under sub-section (1) or sub-
section (5) of this section and|the lapse of every temporary
appointment under sub-section (6) thereof shall be published
in the Gazette.

4() Every notary public shall| have and may exercise within
the Federation or within the territory for which he is
appointed, as the case may bel all the powers and functions
which are ordinarily exercised by notaries public in

5. If it shall appear to the Attorney-General that any
person being a notary public

(a) has been struck off! the roll of advocates and
solicitors of the Supreme: Courf or

(b) has exercised any of the functions of a notary
public outside the territory, if any, specified in
his appointment made under sub-section (1) or
sub-section (5) of section 3, the Attorney-General

appointment of such person and shall cause such

6. Any person who exercis¢s, within the Federation, any

7. (1) The Rule Committee may make rules—
(a) for the guidance and control of persons entitled to
exercise the functions of a notary public under
this Ordinance;

(b) to fix the fees payable to such notaries;

(c) to fix the fees payable by any person on appoint-
ment as a notary public:

Provided that no guch rule shall require any
fee to be paid in respect of any appointment
as a notary public deemed to have been made

(dy by virtue of sub-section (1) of section 8.

(2) All rules made under this section shall be published
in the Gazette, and shall come into force on the date of such
publication or on such later date as may be specified in the
rules.

8. (1) Any person who immediately before the com-
mencement of this Ordinance was lawfully entitled to
practise as a notary public within the Federation or any
territory therein (other than a| person entitled to practise
as a notary public in the State of Johore by virtue of the
provisions of section 4 of the |Notaries Public Ordinance,
1947) shall be deemed to have been appointed a notary
public in accordance with hs Ord to practise as a
notary public within the Federation or (if he was entitled
to practise only within a particular territory in the
Federation) within such territory as the case may be.

(2) If a person was entitled to practise as a notary public
immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance
by virtue of an appointment made under sub-section (5) of
section 3 of the Notaries Public Ordinance; 1947, such
appointment shall lapse at such time as it would have lapsed
if the said Ordinance had not been repealed.

(3) The name of every person who has been deemed to
have been appointed a notady public by virtue of the
provisions of sub-section (1) of this section shall, within
three months of the coming into force of this Ordinance,
or such longer period as the Attorney-General may in any
particular case permit, be published in the Gazette; and
such publication shall be conclusive evidence of the right
of every such person to practise as a notary public under
the provisions of this section. |

9. (1) The Notaries. Publi¢ Ordinance, 1947, is hereby
repealed.

(2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the said Ordinance any
Tules made thereunder and in| force immediately before the
Commencement of this Ordinlance shall, so far as they are
not inconsistent with this Ordinance, be deemed to have
been made under this Ordinance, and shall continue in
force until revoked or repealed by rules made under this
Ordinance, and shall, unless the context otherwise requires,
apply and have effect throughout the Federation.
